rows.stem: The products obtained when Lead nitrate is heated in a boiling tube.
rows.solution:
On heating, lead nitrate decomposes. Brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide are given off, oxygen is released, and lead oxide is left behind:

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

Check: Pb 2 = 2; N 4 = 4; O 12 = 2 + 8 + 2.

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{NO_2}\), \(\mathrm{PbO}\) and \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

rows.stem: Identify a group of the unsaturated hydrocarbons from the following :
rows.solution:
Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon double or triple bond. Ethene (\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2}\)) has a double bond, and propyne (\(\mathrm{CH_3C{\equiv}CH}\)) and butyne (\(\mathrm{C_4H_6}\)) have triple bonds, so all three are unsaturated. Propane, hexane, methane, ethane and cyclohexane contain only single bonds, so they are saturated, and every other group contains at least one of them.

This is option (D) Butyne, Ethene, Propyne.

rows.stem: Select from the following a plant hormone which promotes cell division.
rows.solution:
Cytokinins promote cell division, so they are present in greater concentration where cell division is rapid, as in fruits and seeds. (Auxins and gibberellins promote growth by cell elongation, and abscisic acid inhibits growth.)

This is option (D) Cytokinins.

rows.stem: Offsprings formed as a result of sexual reproduction produce more variations because

options.label: A
options.text: genetic material is contributed by many parents.

options.label: B
options.text: sexual reproduction is a lengthy process.

options.label: C
options.text: genetic material is contributed by two individuals of same species to produce a new generation.

options.label: D
options.text: DNA copying is not accompanied by the creation of cellular apparatus.

rows.solution:
In sexual reproduction two individuals of the same species each contribute half the genetic material, through their gametes, to the offspring. Combining DNA from two different individuals produces new combinations of variations, so the offspring show more variation than offspring copied from a single parent.

This is option (C) genetic material is contributed by two individuals of same species to produce a new generation.

rows.stem: Sex determination depends upon the environment in
rows.solution:
In some reptiles, such as turtles and crocodiles, the sex of the young is decided by the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept, that is, by the environment. In birds and in human beings the sex is decided genetically, by the sex chromosomes.

This is option (C) Reptiles.

rows.stem: In the given circuit the total resistance between X and Y is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the network is given only as a drawing: resistors of 2, 3 and 6 ohm drawn in a row between terminals X and Y, a cell and a key, and two extra connecting wires that bridge parts of the row; where those wires join, and so how the three resistors are combined, is what the question tests and is withheld here. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
In the drawing, the three resistors \(2\,\Omega\), \(3\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\) lie in a row from X to Y. One connecting wire joins X to the junction between the \(3\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\) resistors, and another joins the junction between the \(2\,\Omega\) and \(3\,\Omega\) resistors to Y.

So each resistor has one end at X and the other end at Y: the \(2\,\Omega\) resistor runs from X to a point joined to Y, the \(3\,\Omega\) resistor from that point to a point joined to X, and the \(6\,\Omega\) resistor from there to Y. All three are connected in parallel between X and Y:

\(\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{3 + 2 + 1}{6} = 1\), so \(R = 1\,\Omega\).

This is option (D) \(1\,\Omega\).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Producers are capable of using light energy from the sun to make food available in an ecosystem.

**Reason (R) :** All food chains in an ecosystem start with a producer.
rows.context: Q. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Producers (green plants and blue-green algae) make food from simple inorganic substances using the energy of sunlight, and this food is available to all the other organisms of the ecosystem, so the Assertion is true. Every food chain does begin with a producer, so the Reason is also true. But the Reason does not explain how producers use light energy to make food.

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
(a) Write the essential conditions for following reaction to take place and name its types :

\(\mathrm{2AgCl \longrightarrow 2Ag + Cl_2}\)

(b) Complete the following chemical reaction in the form of a balanced equation :

\(\mathrm{FeSO_4}\) \(\xrightarrow{\Delta}\) \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) + ...... + ......
rows.solution:
(a) The reaction takes place only in the presence of sunlight (light). White silver chloride turns grey as it decomposes into silver and chlorine:

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

It is a decomposition reaction; since light supplies the energy, it is a photochemical (photolytic) decomposition.

(b) On heating, ferrous sulphate gives ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide:

\(\mathrm{2FeSO_4(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Fe_2O_3(s) + SO_2(g) + SO_3(g)}\)

Check: Fe 2 = 2; S 2 = 1 + 1; O 8 = 3 + 2 + 3.

rows.stem:
Give reasons for the following :

(a) Food web is more stable than a food chain in an ecosystem.

(b) A food chain should not have more than four to five trophic levels.
rows.solution:
(a) A food web has many interconnected food chains, so at each trophic level an organism has several alternative sources of food. If one species declines, its consumers can feed on another, so the ecosystem is not disturbed as much as when a single link of a food chain is lost.

(b) Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes on to the next (the ten percent law). After four or five levels the energy left is too little to support another level of organisms, so food chains generally have only three or four steps.

rows.stem: Name the chemical reaction that occurs between iron (III) oxide and aluminium metal. Write its balanced chemical equation. Why is this reaction called displacement reaction ? Give one use of this reaction.
rows.solution:
The reaction of iron(III) oxide with aluminium is the thermit reaction:

\(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow 2Fe(l) + Al_2O_3(s) + heat}\)

It is a displacement reaction because aluminium, being more reactive than iron, displaces iron from its oxide.

So much heat is given out that the iron is produced in the molten state. This is used to join railway tracks and cracked machine parts (thermit welding).

rows.stem:
A student is working in a laboratory with metal ‘E’ which is stored under kerosene oil. Some how a small piece of this metal falls in a beaker containing water and starts burning.

(i) Name the metal ‘E’.

(ii) Write chemical equation for the reaction when metal ‘E’ reacts with water. State the nature (acidic/basic/neutral) of the product obtained.

(iii) Name the process by which this metal ‘E’ is obtained from its molten chloride.
rows.solution:
(i) The metal E is sodium. It is so reactive that it is stored under kerosene to keep it away from air and moisture. (Potassium, also stored under kerosene and catching fire in water, is equally acceptable.)

(ii) Sodium reacts violently with cold water, giving sodium hydroxide and hydrogen; so much heat is released that the hydrogen catches fire:

\(\mathrm{2Na(s) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + H_2(g) + heat\ energy}\)

The product, sodium hydroxide, is basic.

(iii) Sodium is obtained from its molten chloride by electrolytic reduction (electrolysis): sodium is deposited at the cathode and chlorine is set free at the anode.

rows.stem:
State reasons for the following :

(a) Zinc oxide is an amphoteric oxide.

(b) Calcium starts floating when immersed in water.

(c) In the reactions of nitric acid with metals, generally hydrogen gas is not evolved.
rows.solution:
(a) Zinc oxide reacts with both acids and bases to give a salt and water, so it is amphoteric:

\(\mathrm{ZnO + 2HCl \rightarrow ZnCl_2 + H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{ZnO + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2O}\) (sodium zincate)

(b) Calcium reacts with water less violently than sodium, giving calcium hydroxide and hydrogen:

\(\mathrm{Ca(s) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq) + H_2(g)}\)

The bubbles of hydrogen gas formed stick to the surface of the metal, which makes it lighter, so it starts floating.

(c) Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and is itself reduced to oxides of nitrogen, so hydrogen gas is not evolved. (Magnesium and manganese do give hydrogen with very dilute nitric acid.)

rows.stem: Write the name and location of a hormone which helps a person to respond when chased by a dog. Mention the responses in the body which help him to deal with the situation.
rows.solution:
The hormone is adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys. It is secreted directly into the blood and carried to the different parts of the body.

Responses that help him deal with the situation:

1. The heart beats faster, so more oxygen is supplied to the muscles.

2. The blood supply to the digestive system and the skin is reduced, because the muscles around the small arteries in these organs contract; the blood is diverted to the skeletal muscles.

3. The breathing rate increases because of contractions of the diaphragm and the rib muscles.

All these responses prepare the body to run or to fight.

rows.stem:
Draw a schematic diagram of a circuit consisting of a battery of four dry cells of 1.5 V each, a \(2\,\Omega\) resistor, a \(6\,\Omega\) resistor, \(16\,\Omega\) resistor and a plug key all connected in series. Put an ammeter to measure the current in the circuit and a voltmeter across the \(16\,\Omega\) resistor to measure potential difference across its two ends. Use Ohm’s law to determine

(a) ammeter reading, and

(b) voltmeter reading when key is closed.
rows.solution:
Circuit diagram: four cells of \(1{\cdot}5\) V joined in series form the battery. The \(2\,\Omega\), \(6\,\Omega\) and \(16\,\Omega\) resistors, the plug key and the ammeter are all connected in series with the battery, so the same current flows through each. The voltmeter is connected in parallel across the \(16\,\Omega\) resistor only. The positive terminals of the ammeter and the voltmeter are joined towards the positive terminal of the battery.

The battery gives \(V = 4 \times 1{\cdot}5 = 6\) V, and the total resistance in series is \(R = 2 + 6 + 16 = 24\,\Omega\).

(a) By Ohm's law, \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{6}{24} = \dfrac{1}{4} = 0{\cdot}25\) A. The ammeter reads 0.25 A.

(b) The potential difference across the \(16\,\Omega\) resistor is \(V = IR = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 16 = 4\) V. The voltmeter reads 4 V.

rows.stem:
(a) Name any two sexually transmitted diseases.

(b) Prenatal sex determination is prohibited by law. Why ?

(c) Name any three methods of contraception stating one side-effect of each.
rows.solution:
(a) Any two: gonorrhoea, syphilis (bacterial infections); warts, HIV-AIDS (viral infections).

(b) Prenatal sex determination is prohibited because it has been misused for female foeticide, the selective killing of female foetuses. This has made the child sex ratio decline sharply in some parts of the country, and a healthy society needs a balanced ratio of males and females.

(c) Methods with one side-effect each:

1. Oral pills (chemical method): they change the hormonal balance of the body, which can cause side-effects.

2. Copper-T or loop placed in the uterus: it can cause irritation of the uterus.

3. Surgical method (vasectomy in males, tubectomy in females): if not performed properly, it can cause infections and other problems.

rows.stem:
(a) Name a unisexual and a bisexual flower.

(b) Define cross pollination. State how it is carried out.

(c) Observe the diagram given below and name the parts marked as ‘A’ and ‘B’. Mention the function of each of these parts.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (c) asks to name the parts marked 'A' and 'B' on a small boxed drawing of a seed opened into two rounded halves with a small structure between them and two labelled pointers to it; the labels exist only in the drawing and their identities (the answer) are withheld here. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(a) Unisexual flower: papaya (or watermelon). Bisexual flower: *Hibiscus* (or mustard).

(b) Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower (of the same species). It is carried out by pollinating agents such as wind, water and animals (insects and birds).

(c) The drawing shows a seed opened out into its two cotyledons, with the small embryo between them. A, the upper part of the embryo, is the plumule: it develops into the future shoot. B, the lower part, is the radicle: it develops into the future root.
